scope: Official and original methodological sources for clinical evidence-output benchmark design. Research package, not instrument validation.

sources.title: GRADE Working Group: minimal requirements (updated 2023-05)
sources.claim: Certainty is judged for each critical or important outcome; benefits and harms, each relevant GRADE domain, evidence profiles and explicit EtD judgments underpin claims of GRADE use. Recommendations separate direction and strength.
sources.scope: Body of evidence per important outcome; decisions/recommendations use additional EtD criteria.
sources.caveat: GRADE categories are ordinal judgments, not interval numbers; avoid modified GRADE or numerical averaging into a new certainty score.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 14: Summary of findings and GRADE
sources.claim: GRADE uses four certainty categories and considers risk of bias, inconsistency, indirectness, imprecision and publication bias. SoF tables combine effect magnitude, data quantity and certainty.
sources.scope: Outcome-specific synthesis across contributing studies.
sources.caveat: Correctly reporting very-low-certainty evidence is good output quality; a model must not be rewarded merely for choosing high-certainty topics.

sources.title: AGREE II user manual and 23-item instrument
sources.claim: AGREE II contains 23 items across six domains plus two global ratings. At least two and preferably four appraisers are recommended. The consortium sets no universal minimum domain-score threshold.
sources.scope: Methodological development quality and reporting of a guideline document.
sources.caveat: Domain scores should remain distinct. A benchmark pass threshold is a new protocol choice, not an AGREE-endorsed cutoff; an answer-only product cannot be treated as a complete guideline.

sources.title: RIGHT Statement official website
sources.claim: RIGHT describes 22 essential reporting items spanning guideline information, background, evidence, recommendations, review, funding/interests and other information.
sources.scope: Reporting of healthcare practice guidelines.
sources.caveat: The official site states RIGHT is not a quality-assessment instrument for guideline quality; completeness does not establish clinical correctness.

sources.title: AMSTAR 2 original instrument paper
sources.claim: AMSTAR 2 assesses systematic reviews including randomized or nonrandomized intervention studies using 16 items and critical-domain weaknesses. Authors explicitly reject deriving an overall numerical score.
sources.scope: Methodological appraisal of a completed systematic review of healthcare interventions.
sources.caveat: Store original High/Moderate/Low/Critically low judgments, with rationale and critical flaws. Do not call item percentages an AMSTAR2 total or apply it to an isolated short clinical answer.

sources.title: ROBIS official resources, University of Bristol
sources.claim: ROBIS assesses risk of bias in systematic reviews, distinct from risk of bias in primary studies.
sources.scope: Systematic-review processes and conclusions.
sources.caveat: Keep eligibility/relevance and review-level bias judgments separate from source-study bias; neither a citation count nor reporting completeness substitutes for ROBIS.

sources.title: RoB 2 original paper
sources.claim: RoB2 assesses a specific intervention-effect estimate for a particular outcome, endpoint and estimand in a randomized trial.
sources.scope: A single numerical result, not a whole paper/trial uniformly.
sources.caveat: Timepoint, outcome, ITT/per-protocol and design variants matter. Do not assign one whole-trial score mechanically to all results.

sources.title: Cochrane: About risk of bias 2
sources.claim: Cochrane clarifies the result-level nature of RoB2 and recommends concentrating assessments on key outcomes/comparisons used in SoF tables.
sources.scope: Quantitative results contributing to meta-analysis or synthesis without meta-analysis.
sources.caveat: A benchmark wanting exhaustive claim review still needs to predefine which results require formal RoB2 and resource the assessment.

sources.title: ROBINS-I V2 official tool page
sources.claim: The official page identifies a revised ROBINS-I V2 dated 20 November 2025, still a draft subject to change, for specific intervention results in follow-up/cohort studies.
sources.scope: Nonrandomized intervention result; current V2 follow-up/cohort scope.
sources.caveat: Freeze tool version and document date; do not silently mix 2016, Nov2024 and Nov2025 judgments. Website states CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 for RoB2, ROBINS-I, ROBINS-E and ROB-ME; preserve originals and review intended licensing.

sources.title: PRISMA 2020 official statement
sources.claim: PRISMA2020 provides reporting checklists and flow templates for original and updated systematic reviews.
sources.scope: Completeness and transparency of systematic-review reporting.
sources.caveat: Reporting guidance is not a conduct or methodological-quality appraisal; keep PRISMA adherence separate from AMSTAR2/ROBIS.

sources.title: PRISMA 2020 original statement paper
sources.claim: The statement explicitly says PRISMA2020 should not assess review conduct or methodological quality.
sources.scope: Systematic review reporting.
sources.caveat: Do not equate a complete checklist with trustworthy estimates.

sources.title: PRISMA-Search / PRISMA-S official page
sources.claim: The searching extension published in 2021 contains 16 reporting items, including reproducible search documentation.
sources.scope: Search reporting in systematic reviews.
sources.caveat: A reported query/date is auditable transparency, not empirical proof of recall; benchmark retrieval against an adjudicated eligible corpus.

sources.title: WHO handbook for guideline development, 2nd edition
sources.claim: WHO supplies a stepwise process for planning, developing and publishing guidelines, with supplementary chapters on decisions, tests and complexity.
sources.scope: Guideline governance and development workflow.
sources.caveat: A generated recommendation is not a WHO-style guideline without the requisite panel, evidence review, conflict management and contextual judgments. The 2014 publication date must remain visible.

sources.title: NICE guideline manual, introduction
sources.claim: NICE manual shown as updated 23 October 2025 covers development, maintenance and updating, including evidence reviews, economics, committee recommendations and independent quality assurance.
sources.scope: Clinical care, public health and social-care guidelines.
sources.caveat: NICE recommendations include context and value judgments; agreement with one guideline is not a universal clinical truth label across regions.

sources.title: NICE manual Chapter 6, reviewing evidence
sources.claim: NICE describes eight review steps: protocol, identification/selection, appraisal, extraction, synthesis, certainty assessment, interpretation and health inequalities.
sources.scope: Guideline-supporting evidence reviews.
sources.caveat: Review evidence summaries should be distinct from committee interpretation; record deviations and justified reuse of prior review material.

sources.title: NICE manual Chapter 9, interpreting evidence
sources.claim: Recommendations take account of benefits/harms, certainty, preferences, economics, feasibility and equality; evidence requires interpretation.
sources.scope: Recommendation formulation and contextualization.
sources.caveat: A stronger effect or higher certainty alone does not determine a recommendation. Distinguish evidence agreement from judgment agreement.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 22, prospective accumulation
sources.claim: Living reviews require frequent surveillance and timely incorporation of new evidence, rather than merely a recent publication date.
sources.scope: Living systematic reviews.
sources.caveat: Example monthly frequencies in guidance are illustrative, not universal SLA requirements. Track separate discovery, appraisal and incorporation times.

sources.title: Cochrane guidance for living systematic reviews, December 2019
sources.claim: Living status requires continual surveillance, continual status updates and an explicit approach to updating the review itself.
sources.scope: Living intervention-review lifecycle.
sources.caveat: Public freshness labels need audit logs and declared surveillance coverage; not every new study warrants a changed conclusion.

sources.title: Cochrane MECIR C42: collating multiple reports
sources.claim: Multiple reports from one study must be collated so that the study is the review unit.
sources.scope: Study identity and report linkage.
sources.caveat: Count reports, effect rows, participant cohorts and independent studies separately; shared controls/repeated follow-up also require dependence handling.

sources.title: Cochrane Handbook Chapter 10, meta-analysis
sources.claim: Meta-analysis combines sufficiently compatible study results; heterogeneity, effect-scale selection and sensitivity analyses require judgment. Random-effects estimates describe an average with prediction intervals where defensible.
sources.scope: Within a clinically and statistically coherent comparison/outcome/timepoint/estimand cell.
sources.caveat: Never pool unrelated diseases or outcomes into a universal treatment effect. Small-k heterogeneity and prediction intervals are uncertain.

sources.title: QUADAS-3 official University of Bristol page
sources.claim: Official page recommends QUADAS-3 for test-accuracy reviews, published February 2026; latest downloadable version shown as 1.2. It moves assessment to estimate level.
sources.scope: Accuracy studies for diagnosis, screening or staging.
sources.caveat: Use current QUADAS3 module, not a default QUADAS2 template. Preserve the downloaded version and clarify synthesis questions/ideal test-accuracy study.

sources.title: PROBAST+AI original instrument paper
sources.claim: PROBAST+AI updates appraisal for regression/AI prediction models, separates development quality from bias in performance evaluation, and considers applicability and fairness.
sources.scope: Prediction model development and apparent/internal/external performance evaluation.
sources.caveat: This appraises evidence about prediction models; it is not a generic score for the trustworthiness of an LLM answer.

sources.title: ROBINS-E official tool page
sources.claim: ROBINS-E version 24 March 2024 addresses effects of exposures in observational epidemiological follow-up studies.
sources.scope: Environmental, occupational and behavioural exposure results.
sources.caveat: Useful for broad-health causal claims; not interchangeable with ROBINS-I intervention appraisal or with mere association extraction.

sources.title: GRADE-CERQual official approach
sources.claim: CERQual assesses confidence in each qualitative synthesis finding using methodological limitations, coherence, adequacy and relevance.
sources.scope: Qualitative review findings about experience, barriers, acceptability or implementation.
sources.caveat: Qualitative findings do not need a numeric treatment effect; retain finding-specific categorical confidence.

sources.title: Australian Living Evidence Collaboration: Living Guidelines Handbook v1.1, Aug2025
sources.claim: A living guideline comprises living recommendations updated as information becomes available, supported by continuing evidence surveillance.
sources.scope: Living recommendation lifecycle.
sources.caveat: Surveillance, review and recommendation revision are separate processes; publish explicit no-change decisions as well as changed versions.

sources.title: Cochrane Methods Report 2026, published 16 September 2026
sources.claim: Cochrane reports RAISE version4 released in early March2026 with updated AI taxonomy and responsible-handover guidance. It reports CESAR protocol publication and expected results later in2026.
sources.scope: Current responsible-AI framework and methods status.
sources.caveat: Version4 release is verified through Cochrane; OSF direct page returned403, so full RAISE4 questionnaire content was not independently retrieved.

sources.title: RAISE project / Responsible use of AI in evidence synthesis
sources.claim: RAISE is the responsible-AI framework linked from Cochrane's2026 report; v4 early March2026 is identified by Cochrane.
sources.scope: Responsible handover, tool selection, validation, disclosure and oversight.
sources.caveat: OSF direct access403. Do not imply all current recommendations were read directly; use Cochrane's account and retrieve/freeze actual v4 documents before instrument implementation.

sources.title: Cochrane: Right tool, right job, 15June2026
sources.claim: Four expectations are author responsibility, preserved methodological rigor/integrity, transparent reporting and human oversight. Selection examines purpose, data provenance, contextual validation, usability and transparency; context-specific performance thresholds lack community consensus.
sources.scope: Practical implementation of RAISE3 and tool-use decisions.
sources.caveat: This is implementation guidance, not clinical validation of every tool. CESAR stopping thresholds shown there belong to that study and must not be presented as universal acceptable-performance cutoffs.

sources.title: Cochrane: What makes the new AI study innovative, 17April2026
sources.claim: CESAR embeds AI-tool comparisons in roughly15Cochrane review updates, using an adaptive platform SWAR allowing additions/removals of tools and examining downstream errors, accuracy, stability, efficiency and usability.
sources.scope: Prospective workflow evaluation rather than one-time static tests.
sources.caveat: The April post describes a study/protocol and novelty claims by its authors, not completed outcome evidence or a validated universal benchmark.

sources.title: CESAR protocol, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology, doi10.1016/j.jclinepi.2026.112390
sources.claim: The protocol specifies a master adaptive platform SWAR comparing tools with human-only processes for title/abstract screening, full-text screening and extraction. Evaluations include accuracy, time, response stability, error impacts and usability.
sources.scope: Task and workflow validation in ongoing reviews.
sources.caveat: Protocol publication is not proof of performance; cite study status accurately. Publisher full text returned403; author repository abstract and accepted-manuscript metadata were accessible.

sources.title: UCL author repository: CESAR protocol record
sources.claim: Repository confirms JCE Article112390, DOI, accepted version available and study design; describes the comparator as two trained researchers independently completing each step.
sources.scope: Primary author-repository record supporting CESAR design.
sources.caveat: Record labels article Inpress. Main benchmark reference should additionally use independently adjudicated disagreements and clinicians/methodologists for material issues; that adjudication policy is our proposal, not a quoted CESAR requirement.

evaluation_units.definition: Atomic verifiable factual or causal statement with eligible source support and scope.
Study identity × outcome × comparison × endpoint × estimand × analysis variant; links all reports and data provenance.
Population × intervention/exposure × comparator × outcome × time window × design/estimand; k counts independent contributing study units after overlap handling.
Decision with direction, strength, conditions, target population, certainty, EtD rationale and jurisdiction.
Whole evidence answer/review/guideline package/version, with a declared task track and resource envelope.

guideline_pipeline: Scope, population, users and jurisdiction; priority questions and patient-important outcomes.
Protocol, methods and conflicts; multidisciplinary panel and patient/public involvement.
Reproducible search and selection, report-to-study linkage and exclusion reasons.
Result-level extraction, appraisal, synthesis and outcome-level certainty.
EtD: benefits/harms, values, resources, equity, acceptability, feasibility and contextual judgment.
Recommendation formulation, transparent rationale, independent quality assurance and consultation.
Publication with provenance, version, search cutoff and declared surveillance/update rules.
Surveillance, triage, adjudication and versioned update or documented no-change decision.

proposed_critical_gates.name: Source integrity
proposed_critical_gates.test: A material claim cites a fabricated, materially misattributed, retracted-without-context or unsupported source.
proposed_critical_gates.outcome: Claim fails; serious safety-critical instances block overall certification.
proposed_critical_gates.status: New benchmark rule; thresholds require prespecification and validation.

proposed_critical_gates.name: Study identity/dependence
proposed_critical_gates.test: Duplicated reports/cohorts/shared controls materially inflate independent k or precision without correction.
proposed_critical_gates.status: New benchmark gate grounded in established methods.

proposed_critical_gates.name: Numerical/causal validity
proposed_critical_gates.test: A material direction, denominator, scale, unit, estimand or causal-design error changes interpretation.
proposed_critical_gates.outcome: Affected estimate/claim fails; publish error taxonomy.
proposed_critical_gates.status: New benchmark gate; clinical materiality adjudicated independently.

proposed_critical_gates.name: Unsafe recommendation/overclaim
proposed_critical_gates.test: Omitted serious contraindication/harm or unsupported recommendation strength materially increases risk.
proposed_critical_gates.outcome: Recommendation fails even if other dimensions are high.
proposed_critical_gates.status: New benchmark gate; not an official GRADE/AGREE pass threshold.

proposed_critical_gates.name: Auditability
proposed_critical_gates.test: No recoverable run/version, source cutoff, source links or evidence-to-claim mapping for an audit-required task.
proposed_critical_gates.outcome: Not auditable; do not certify, while distinguishing unavailable from demonstrably wrong.

proposed_critical_gates.name: Scope and applicability
proposed_critical_gates.test: Evidence is presented as directly applicable outside its studied population/context without acknowledging material indirectness.
proposed_critical_gates.outcome: Claim/recommendation fails applicability review when risk is clinically important.

operational_mapping.metric: Recall/precision against a time-frozen, adjudicated eligible corpus, sensitivity to missing sentinel studies.
operational_mapping.limit: Search reporting is not measured recall; incomplete reference corpora require uncertainty labels.

operational_mapping.metric: Agreement with independent expert result-level judgments; weighted kappa/ordinal error with rationales, plus critical disagreement review.
operational_mapping.limit: Do not reward high-certainty labels as such; judge whether certainty is justified.

operational_mapping.metric: Native AMSTAR2/ROBIS judgments plus a separately named benchmark performance score for task correctness.
operational_mapping.limit: No AMSTAR sum; risk-of-bias labels remain native categorical judgments.

operational_mapping.metric: Six original AGREEII domain scores, two global judgments, EtD completeness, RIGHT reporting.
operational_mapping.limit: No official universal domain pass/fail threshold; generation alone does not supply a legitimate guideline panel.

operational_mapping.metric: Publication/indexing availability→discovery→eligibility/appraisal→incorporation lags; eligible-new-evidence recall; missed safety update rate.
operational_mapping.limit: Frozen benchmark and prospective living benchmark must remain separate; timely no-change decisions are valid.

operational_mapping.metric: Target-relative population coverage and indirectness, explicitly stratified by age/sex/gender/ethnicity/geography/setting.
operational_mapping.limit: Observed demographic diversity is not proof of effect transportability; missing reporting is unknown, not zero representation.

operational_mapping.metric: Predefined sensitivity analysis and longitudinal changes in effect/clinical decision; perturbations must include removal of influential/high-bias studies.
operational_mapping.limit: Stability alone is not accuracy; correct reversal after new evidence must be rewarded.

overall_score_caution: A separate proposed 0–100 task-performance index can be piloted after prespecifying weights and noncompensable gates. Label it experimental. Do not present it as GRADE, AMSTAR2 or AGREE certification, and do not conflate evidence-base certainty, evidence-base demographic completeness and the producer’s quality of work.
human_reference_process: Two independent trained reviewers per key claim/result/cell; third expert adjudication; topic clinician and methods/statistics input for material disagreements. Report reviewer agreement and both reference uncertainty and system uncertainty. Source labels made by an LLM remain draft judgments until adjudicated.
licensing_note: Only concise paraphrases and links are reproduced here, not full copyrighted instruments. Check current instrument permissions before bundling questionnaires or commercializing derivative implementations.

RAISE_CESAR_integration.principle: Use RAISE4 as current responsible-AI framework after obtaining and freezing actual files; use CESAR adaptive SWAR as the closest methodological template for prospective task/workflow evaluation.
requirements: Tool purpose, version, data provenance, intended workflow role, resource envelope and human supervision are recorded.
Evaluate standalone outputs and human+AI workflows separately; retain same task, source corpus, cutoff and budgets where compared.
Prespecify accuracy, error-impact, response-stability, efficiency/usability metrics and stopping/noninferiority criteria before system outputs are unblinded.
Do not reuse CESAR study-specific thresholds as medical consensus.
A human reference panel independently reviews and adjudicates; LLMs can assist triage but do not act as sole ground-truth judges.
Hold public dev and private heldout/prospective temporal splits, retiring leaked tasks without retrospectively rewriting scores.
Downstream change in synthesized effects, certainty and recommendations must be measured, not only extraction cell accuracy.
RAISE_CESAR_integration.status_caveat: Sources describe ongoing methods guidance and study protocols. No CESAR tool performance results or benchmark validation are inferred.
